current.text: Toronto traded for Kawhi Leonard, who takes the place of Brandon Ingram.
He is a projected starter next to Quickley, Barrett, Leonard and Poeltl. He is also in the expected closing five.
Experts doubt he takes a big step forward this season. Kawhi Leonard is better and uses more possessions, so a jump in usage is harder.
He should not lose touches with Kawhi on the team, because his value comes through facilitation.
Experts value him around picks 12 to 17 in 9-cat, so a late first or early second round pick. ESPN's rank of 10 is too high. An ESPN ADP of 31 is too late.
Toronto has 15 back-to-backs this season and three of them fall in the fantasy playoffs.

durable.text: He is one of the best help rim protectors in the league and anchors Toronto's defense.
His shooting is a question mark.
He does not need high usage to produce. Much of his value comes from facilitation.
He helps in many categories. His assists and steals are far above other forwards and centers, and his blocks and rebounds are also above average. Turnovers are his weak category.

note: Experts put Barnes around picks 12 to 17 in 9-cat. That matches Yahoo's 42 USD value and 46.2 USD average cost better than ESPN's 55 USD, and it is well above the 31 USD he cost in our league last season, so a fair price is about 40 to 46 USD. He fits punt TO and Giannis punt FT% builds and gives frontcourt assists, steals and blocks. Early in the season, check how he shares the ball with Kawhi and whether his shooting holds. Last season his FG% rose to 50.7 while his threes fell to 0.8 per game.
